references.text: The Lord commands Moses to consecrate the people before He reveals Himself on Mount Sinai, just as Joshua commands the people to consecrate themselves before the Lord's miraculous deeds.
Moses consecrated the people before they met the Lord, just as Joshua now does before crossing over the Jordan.
The command to consecrate oneself because the Lord is holy links together the requirement for holiness before God's acts.
The people were asked to consecrate themselves before eating the meat the Lord would give them.
Moses' song praises the Lord's miraculous deeds, which Joshua now promises the Lord will do among the people.
The Lord promises to perform miracles (נִפְלָאֹת) never seen before, using the same word that Joshua uses.
Samuel asked the people to consecrate themselves before an offering to the Lord, the same command for holiness before meeting with God.
David urged the people to consecrate themselves for the Lord, the same call to holiness before serving God.
The Levites consecrated those who were unclean among the people, showing the necessity of holiness before worship.
Job consecrated his children, illustrating the practice of consecrating oneself before appearing before the Lord.
